Split a Chromosome Set into Window-Scan Chunks

Source: R/define_genome_chunks.R
define_genome_chunks.Rd

Builds the chunk lookup table for the genomic-chunk SLURM array that drives a sliding-window GLOW scan. Each chunk is one array task; the table maps SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to a chromosome and a contiguous run of window start positions.

define_genome_chunks(
  chrom_spans,
  window_size,
  step_size,
  chunk_strategy = "fixed_mb",
  chunk_size_mb = 5,
  gds_paths = NULL
)

Arguments

chrom_spans

A data.frame with columns chr, start, end — one row per chromosome, giving its inclusive position extent (typically the per-chr GDS min/max position, computed during preparation). Rows are processed in genomic order regardless of input order.

window_size

Integer window width in bp (e.g. 100000L).

step_size

Integer step between consecutive window starts (e.g. 10000L). Governs the window count.

chunk_strategy

Character. Only "fixed_mb" is supported in v1; any other value is an error.

chunk_size_mb

Numeric chunk width in Mb (default 5, the STAARpipeline-proven value). Must be large enough to hold at least one step (chunk_size_mb * 1e6 >= step_size).

gds_paths

Reserved for a future variant-count-balancing strategy; unused in v1 ("fixed_mb").

Value

A data.frame, one row per chunk in genomic order, with columns:

chunk_id

Integer, 1-based global id; the scan selects its chunk by SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID == chunk_id.

chr

Chromosome label.

chunk_start

Integer, inclusive lower bound of owned window starts (grid-aligned). Passed as define_regions_window's start.

chunk_end

Integer, inclusive upper bound of owned window starts; the scan keeps windows with start <= chunk_end.

span_end

Integer, the chromosome's max position; passed as define_regions_window's end so boundary-spanning windows are generated and window ends are capped at the chromosome extent.

est_n_windows

Integer, the number of window starts owned by the chunk (exact for fixed geometry; for SLURM load inspection).

Details

Boundary rule. A window is owned by the chunk containing its start. Chunks own contiguous runs of windows_per_chunk = floor(chunk_size_mb * 1e6 / step_size) positions on the per-chromosome step grid (anchored at the span start), so chunk_start is always a grid-aligned window start and the union of all chunks' windows equals one full-span slide — no duplicates, no gaps. The scan builds a chunk's windows with define_regions_window(chr, chunk_start, span_end, window_size, step_size) and keeps rows with start <= chunk_end; generating to span_end (not chunk_end) lets a window start in the chunk and spill past its end, matching the full-span slide. span_end is returned for that one lookup.

For configs where step_size divides chunk_size_mb * 1e6 (the usual case, e.g. 5 Mb / 10 kb), chunk_start/chunk_end equal the naive fixed-Mb boundaries; otherwise chunks are rounded down to a whole number of steps to keep the grid aligned.

See also

GLOWr::define_regions_window, glow_scan_chunk()

Examples

spans <- data.frame(chr = c("21", "22"),
                    start = c(1L, 1L),
                    end = c(12000000L, 8000000L))
chunks <- define_genome_chunks(spans, window_size = 100000L,
                               step_size = 10000L, chunk_size_mb = 5)
chunks
#>   chunk_id chr chunk_start chunk_end span_end est_n_windows
#> 1        1  21           1   5000000 12000000           500
#> 2        2  21     5000001  10000000 12000000           500
#> 3        3  21    10000001  12000000 12000000           191
#> 4        4  22           1   5000000  8000000           500
#> 5        5  22     5000001   8000000  8000000           291
